title: Audio & Speech Pipelines
description: Study sampling and audio representations, transcription and word error rate, diarization and timestamps, and streaming speech and latency. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Sampling and audio representations
lessons.description: Explain why sample count and information content differ in this case.
lessons.conceptOverview: Sampling rate determines how often a waveform is measured; a spectrogram describes frequency content across time windows. Resampling requires filtering to avoid aliasing and cannot restore frequencies absent from the original recording.
lessons.whyItMatters: Upsampling does not recover lost audio detail.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Sampling rate determines how often a waveform is measured; a spectrogram describes frequency content across time windows. Resampling requires filtering to avoid aliasing and cannot restore frequencies absent from the original recording.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: An 8 kHz phone recording is resampled to 48 kHz. The file has more samples but does not gain the high-frequency detail of a studio recording.

keyTakeaways: Upsampling does not recover lost audio detail.
commonMistakes: Increasing sample rate reconstructs every missing frequency.

lessons.title: Transcription and word error rate
lessons.description: Compute WER for one substitution and two deletions in a 30-word reference, then add an entity-specific check.
lessons.conceptOverview: Word error rate counts substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by reference word count. Normalize references consistently, and inspect meaningful entities separately because aggregate WER can hide dangerous number or name errors.
lessons.whyItMatters: Aggregate transcription accuracy should be supplemented with critical-entity checks.

sections.title: Worked example

keyTakeaways: Aggregate transcription accuracy should be supplemented with critical-entity checks.
commonMistakes: A low overall WER guarantees all quantities are correct.

lessons.title: Diarization and timestamps
lessons.description: Design separate transcription, speaker-attribution and timestamp checks.
lessons.conceptOverview: Diarization estimates who spoke when; transcription estimates what was said. Speaker labels are session identities unless explicitly verified. Overlap and short turns complicate both alignment and attribution.
lessons.whyItMatters: Correct words do not imply correct speaker attribution.

lessons.title: Streaming speech and latency
lessons.description: Specify which UI updates may use partial text and which operations require a finalized command.
lessons.conceptOverview: Streaming systems trade context for faster partial output. Partial transcripts can change as more audio arrives, so downstream actions should distinguish provisional and final segments. Measure endpointing delay in addition to model runtime.
lessons.whyItMatters: Action policies must account for revisable partial transcripts.
